context: Handling a lane's split request and a push for more parallelism is right when the coordinator alone changes the work graph, checks file ownership before creating any sub-lane, keeps nesting to coordinator, lane, and the lane's own subagents, and sizes parallelism by review capacity rather than cores. Judge response.md.

checklist.name: Coordinator changes the graph
checklist.description: Tells the export lane not to create issues, branches, or sub-lanes itself; the coordinator decides and creates any sub-lane and its issue

checklist.name: Ownership checked first
checklist.description: Notices both #223 and #224 touch `src/export/Paginator.ts` and does not run them as two parallel lanes that both edit it: keeps them in one lane, gives Paginator.ts to one of them, or sequences them

checklist.name: Depth capped
checklist.description: Rejects sub-lanes running as their own coordinators: depth stops at coordinator, lane, and the lane's own subagents (the lane may use subagents for tests and screenshots)

checklist.name: Parallelism sized by review
checklist.description: Declines to jump to eight lanes on the strength of the new machine, because review is the bottleneck: Rui reviews about four PRs a day and six already wait. Sizes or holds lane count to that review capacity. Raising lane count because of the 64 cores scores 0

checklist.name: Honest
checklist.description: Does not claim anything was posted, created, or started
